correctness.rationale: For each ordered word of r independent binary row indices, composing exact complex reflections yields the alternating-sign exponent S and its full binomial law. Even r: the half-average is multiplication by e^{iSθ}cos(Sθ), so zero occurs exactly at an integer-angle resonance and first hit is geometric. Odd r: the half-average is P onto the virtual line L_{Sθ}; after the first surviving step, zero occurs iff consecutive axes are perpendicular. Positive support on each integer in an interval of width r gives a necessary-and-sufficient resonance condition and almost-sure stopping by independent disjoint pair trials. Reduced-denominator arithmetic gives the sharp r cutoffs. The killed substochastic matrix yields the generic initial survival distribution and finite expected hitting time; explicit rational inversions give 61/9 and 36. Standalone exact symbolic matrix checker verifies 508 full reflection-word identities at two benchmark angles and the rational Markov computations. General statements are proved analytically, not inferred from tests.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For an odd-length reflection word, its half-average becomes an orthogonal projection onto a line indexed by an alternating binomial word sum; exact absorption then depends on perpendicular consecutive virtual lines. These separate mechanisms and their binomial supports are not given by a standard fixed-two-line iteration formula.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns almost-sure exact finite hitting times of fresh uniformly sampled reflection bundles on two planar equations, with sharp parity and rational-angle denominator thresholds and an explicit killed-transition Markov law. The source develops the same randomized operator but provides expectation/mean-iterate convergence bounds rather than finite-step hitting classification. Material inspection of the cited fixed two-set Douglas–Rachford finite convergence and two-line rate papers found distinct dynamics. Record searches for aliases, orthogonal virtual projections, integer angle resonances, random reflection words and hitting times did not locate a stronger implication. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent formulations remains.
residual_risks: Semantic searches and inspected texts cannot prove absolute bibliographic uniqueness; a specialized unindexed random alternating-projection formulation may exist.
Bibliographic comparison is not an independent audit; no empirical floating-point stopping claim is intended.

value.rationale: An expectation-convergent randomized feasibility algorithm can have either zero probability of exact finite success or probability one, according to a dense arithmetic condition on the planar row angle. The theorem specifies the sharp parity-sensitive minimum reflection budget, resolves exact finite hitting for all block lengths and angles in its domain, and determines a nontrivial first-passage distribution and resource-cost comparison (61/3 versus 32 row reflections at π/4). Exact stopping and robustness boundaries matter for whether finite arithmetic termination is possible in this projection method, beyond textbook contraction estimates; the explicit nonrobustness to angle perturbation is disclosed.
